{"codepoint":"U+5B6C","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Nao","reason":"Every cited Unihan field and MOE give nāo, and no source supports Huai. Huai looks like the pronunciation of 坏, a semantic gloss for 'bad', not a reading of 孬. Pinyin ASCII fold nao."},
{"codepoint":"U+5BE7","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Ning","reason":"Unihan and MOE give níng/nìng, both of which fold to Ning. Zhu is the reading of 宁 U+5B81 (zhù), which is also this character's simplified variant, so the value probably leaked in through the variant mapping. It is not a reading of 寧."},
{"codepoint":"U+60DA","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Hu","reason":"kMandarin, kHanyuPinlu, kTGHZ2013 and MOE all give hū, and Cantonese fat1 and fanqie 呼骨 point to an h-initial reading. Bu has no support, so this is a wrong consonant."},
{"codepoint":"U+6251","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Pu","reason":"kMandarin and MOE give pū, and the Unihan secondary reading is pì, so the initial is p-, not b-. Bu is a wrong consonant (aspirated vs unaspirated). The accepted 'pi' is only a secondary reading."},
{"codepoint":"U+6482","verdict":"prefer_default","suggested":"Liao","reason":"Modern Mandarin default is liào, supported by Unihan, XHC, TGHZ and MOE. Lue is not a random typo: fanqie 離灼 and kJapanese リャク point to a historical lüè-type reading. Treat Lue as a historical alternative, not a confirmed error."},
{"codepoint":"U+65EF","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"La","reason":"All cited fields give lá (as in 旮旯), and Cantonese lo1/lok1 also fits an l-initial. Xu has no support, so this is a wrong consonant and vowel."},
{"codepoint":"U+70C3","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Ting","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE give tīng for 烴, and Cantonese ting1 agrees. Jing is the reading of the phonetic component 巠, so this looks like a component-derived guess that was never attested for the character itself."},
{"codepoint":"U+762A","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Bie","reason":"The readings are biě/biē, which fold to Bie, and Cantonese bit6 agrees. Pie is a wrong consonant (p vs b)."},
{"codepoint":"U+765F","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Bie","reason":"The readings are biě/bié/biē, which fold to Bie, and fanqie 蒲結 and Cantonese bit6 agree. Pie is a wrong consonant. 芳滅 hints at a p- fanqie, but no modern Mandarin source gives pie, so I am not treating it as a valid alternative."},
{"codepoint":"U+7845","verdict":"prefer_default","suggested":"Gui","reason":"The default reading is guī (silicon), corroborated by Unihan, XHC, TGHZ and MOE. Huo is not an exact match for anything cited. The archaic Unihan secondary reading hè and fanqie 虎伯 suggest an h-initial historical reading, so I would not call Huo a clear typo. Uncertain."},
{"codepoint":"U+7C72","verdict":"prefer_default","suggested":"Yu","reason":"All cited sources give yù for 籲, and Cantonese jyu6 agrees. The simplified variant 吁 U+5401 also has the reading xū, which probably explains Xu. Xu is not attested for 籲 itself."},
{"codepoint":"U+7EBC","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Zhen","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (紖) give zhèn. Yin is likely derived from the component 引 (yǐn) and is not attested as a reading of this character. Cantonese can2 is a separate matter and does not support Yin."},
{"codepoint":"U+7ECC","verdict":"prefer_default","suggested":"Chu","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE give chù. Cantonese zyut3 and the semantic link to 拙 (zhuō) make a Zhuo-type reading plausible historically or by contamination, but it is unattested in the cited Mandarin sources. Chu is the modern default."},
{"codepoint":"U+7F9F","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Qiang","reason":"Unihan and MOE give qiǎng, and Cantonese koeng5 has an -ng final. Qian has the wrong final (-n instead of -ng). MOE also lists kēng for the traditional form, but nothing supports Qian."},
{"codepoint":"U+82CE","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Zhu","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (苧) give zhù, and Cantonese cyu5 agrees. Meng has no support in any cited field."},
{"codepoint":"U+859B","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Xue","reason":"Unihan and MOE give xuē (surname Xue), and Cantonese sit3 fits an x-/s- initial. Xie is a wrong vowel, probably confusion with phonetically similar 屑 or 謝."},
{"codepoint":"U+8934","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Lan","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (襤) give lán, and Cantonese laam4 agrees. Bao looks like confusion with 褓 (bǎo). It is not a reading of 褴."},
{"codepoint":"U+8941","verdict":"prefer_default","suggested":"Qiang","reason":"Modern default is qiǎng (Unihan, XHC, TGHZ, MOE), as in 襁褓. Jiang matches the fanqie 居兩 and the Cantonese goeng5 form, so it is a historical/dialect-compatible alternative. Not a confirmed error, but Qiang is the better modern default."},
{"codepoint":"U+9486","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Ga","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (釓) give gá, and Cantonese gaa1 agrees. Qiu has no support."},
{"codepoint":"U+948C","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Liao","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (釕) give liǎo/liào, which fold to Liao, and Cantonese liu5 agrees. Diao is likely confusion with 钓 (diào) and is not attested for this character."},
{"codepoint":"U+9496","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Yang","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (鍚) give yáng, and Cantonese joeng4 agrees. Xi is the reading of 锡/錫 (tin), a different character."},
{"codepoint":"U+94C6","verdict":"prefer_default","suggested":"Mao","reason":"The rivet sense is mǎo (XHC, TGHZ, MOE), and Cantonese maau5 agrees. Liu may reflect an older reading for the same 鉚 form (the 卯 component also reads liǔ in 柳), but I cannot corroborate that from the cited sources. Treat as unverified. Mao is the modern default."},
{"codepoint":"U+94CA","verdict":"prefer_default","suggested":"Ta","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE give tā (thallium), with tuó as a secondary reading. She is not in the cited fields. It may be a historical reading of 鉈 (shé, short spear), which I cannot verify here. Treat as uncertain. Ta is the modern element reading."},
{"codepoint":"U+94EA","verdict":"prefer_default","suggested":"Ha","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (鉿) give hā (hafnium), and Cantonese hap6 agrees. Jia has no support in the cited fields, though an archaic reading of this form cannot be excluded. Uncertain. Ha is the modern default."},
{"codepoint":"U+9507","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"E","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (鋨) give é, and Cantonese ngo4 agrees. Tie probably comes from confusion with 铁/鐵 (iron). Not attested in the cited sources, though a variant relation to 鐵 is not fully ruled out. Pinyin ASCII fold is E."},
{"codepoint":"U+9517","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Zhe","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (鍺) give zhě, and Cantonese ze2 agrees. Duo has no support."},
{"codepoint":"U+9518","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Nuo","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (鍩) give nuò, and Cantonese nok6 agrees. Tian has no support."},
{"codepoint":"U+9536","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Si","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (鍶) give sī, and Cantonese si1 agrees. Song is a wrong vowel and final."},
{"codepoint":"U+9616","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"He","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (闔) give hé, and Cantonese hap6 agrees. Ge is probably contamination from 阁/閣 (gé) or 閤. It is not a reading of 阖 in the cited sources."},
{"codepoint":"U+97A5","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Eng","reason":"Unihan, XHC and MOE give ēng, and Cantonese ang1 agrees. Yi has no support. Eng is a valid ASCII fold of ēng."},
{"codepoint":"U+9CC0","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Ti","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (鯷) give tí, and Cantonese tai4 agrees. Shi looks like a guess from the component 是, with no attestation in the cited sources."},
{"codepoint":"U+9CCF","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Guan","reason":"XHC, TGHZ and MOE (鰥) give guān, and Cantonese gwaan1 agrees. Yin has no support."},
{"codepoint":"U+9EE5","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"Qing","reason":"All cited sources give qíng, fanqie 渠京 gives a q- initial, and Cantonese king4 agrees. Jing is a wrong consonant, probably from the component 京 (jīng)."},
{"codepoint":"U+32D3","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"e","reason":"CIRCLED KATAKANA E decomposes to U+30A8 エ, which romanizes as e. The current 'u' duplicates ㋒ U+32D2. This is a wrong vowel, a straightforward letter typo."},
{"codepoint":"U+33A3","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"mm^3","reason":"SQUARE MM CUBED decomposes to 006D 006D 00B3, so the exponent is 3. The neighboring cm³/m³/km³ entries use ^3. This is an exponent typo and an ASCII-folding fix, not a pronunciation question."},
{"codepoint":"U+3371","verdict":"confirm_error","suggested":"hPa","reason":"SQUARE HPA decomposes to U+0068 U+0050 U+0061, which is hPa. The SI symbol is case-sensitive, so HPA is a case error. This is a compatibility-decomposition ASCII fold, not a pronunciation scheme."}
